title: Brand kit
description: One brand's look and voice for every email the engine renders: logo, colors (light and dark mode), fonts, footer, voice, sender identities and social links. Loaded by engine/render/brand.py, which also checks text contrast against WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 for normal text, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#contrast-minimum). Every field except brand_name is optional; missing values come from the neutral default kit. A filled, commented example is templates/brand/brand.yaml.

brand_name.description: The name people know the brand by, as it should appear in emails.

lang.description: Language of the emails as a BCP 47 tag (en, en-GB, de, fr-CA). Sets the lang attribute screen readers use. Default: en.

website.description: The brand's home page. The logo links here.

logo.description: The logo at the top of every email. Leave it out and emails start with the headline, as the neutral default does.

url.description: A PNG, JPG or GIF on a public https address (no SVG: most email clients do not show it).

alt.description: What the logo says, read aloud by screen readers and shown when images are off. Usually the brand name.

width.description: Display width in pixels. Export the file at twice this width so it stays sharp on high-density screens.

height.description: Display height in pixels. Optional: left out, the height follows the image's proportions.

colors.description: Light-mode colors as #RRGGBB, plus their dark-mode counterparts under dark. Text, link and button-text colors must reach 4.5:1 contrast against what they sit on, in both modes, or the kit is rejected.

background.description: The page around the card, and the footer.

card.description: The content area behind the logo, headline, body and button.

link.description: Links, including the footer links. Default: primary, when it is readable; otherwise text.

dark.description: The same roles in dark mode, applied by clients that support prefers-color-scheme (Apple Mail, iOS Mail, Outlook for Mac, Outlook.com and others). Missing values: primary and button_text keep their light values, text #F2F2F2, background #121212, card #1E1E1E, link the light link when readable, otherwise the dark text.

fonts.description: Typefaces. The stack is what most inboxes show; a web font is an optional extra for the clients that load one (Apple Mail, iOS Mail, some Android apps).

stack.description: A comma-separated web-safe font stack, for example: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif. Outlook for Windows always uses the first font in it.

name.description: The font family name exactly as the stylesheet declares it, for example: Inter.

url.description: The stylesheet address, for example a Google Fonts css2 link.

footer.description: What the footer says. The unsubscribe link is always added by the renderer in the platform's own syntax.

legal_name.description: The registered company name shown before a literal postal address.

postal_address.description: The physical mailing address CAN-SPAM requires. Used when the brief has none and the platform has no address token (Customer.io, Braze).

extra_lines.description: Extra footer sentences, such as why the reader gets this email. {product_name} is filled in.

voice.description: How the brand writes. Handed to the writer with every copy brief and checked after drafting; never rendered on its own.

register.description: The tone in a sentence: plain, specific, second person, no exclamation marks.

vocabulary.description: Words the brand never writes, each with the words it uses instead.

forbidden_phrases.description: Phrases that must never appear in copy.

sign_off.description: How a message signs off when it signs off at all, for example: The Ridgeview team.

senders.description: Who emails come from. marketing is the brand itself; person is a named human for plain, one-to-one style messages.

social.description: Social profiles, shown as text links in the footer (text, not icons, so the email stays readable with images off).

plain_text.description: Words only: no HTML and no template code ({{ }}, {% %}, %% %%, ${ }). The renderer adds the template code for each platform.
